summary: This document describes transporting Ethernet frames, including port-to-port frames and VLAN frames, over L2TPv3. The mechanism can be used to build pseudowires that carry Ethernet across an IP network. It was later updated by RFC 5641.

plainLanguage.summary: Two faraway office networks can be joined as if connected by one cable. This explains how to wrap their Ethernet traffic and carry it through the internet.

questions: what is the l2tpv3 circuit status avp
how does l2tpv3 carry ethernet vlan frames
subtitle: How to carry Ethernet frames across an IP network as an L2TPv3 pseudowire, so two distant LANs act like one link.

tldr.problem: A provider wants to carry Ethernet traffic between two sites over an IP network, as if one Ethernet link joined them.
tldr.mechanism: Each Ethernet port or VLAN is mapped to an L2TPv3 session. The whole frame, minus preamble and FCS, is wrapped in L2TPv3 and sent as one packet, and link status is signalled with the Circuit Status AVP.
tldr.outcome: It gives a port-to-port or VLAN-to-VLAN Ethernet service over IP, but offers no congestion control of its own. RFC 5641 updates it.

today: RFC 4719 is a Proposed Standard published in November 2006 and is updated by RFC 5641. It builds on the L2TPv3 base specification, RFC 3931.

sections.title: Ethernet Pseudowires over L2TPv3
sections.content:
The Layer 2 Tunneling Protocol, Version 3 (L2TPv3) can act as both a control protocol and a data encapsulation to set up pseudowires (PWs) that carry layer 2 data units across an IP network. RFC 4719 describes how to do that for Ethernet frames, covering both PW establishment and the data encapsulation.

An Ethernet PW emulates a single Ethernet link between exactly two endpoints. The RFC uses "Ethernet" loosely, to include protocols reasonably similar to IEEE 802.3 in packet format, such as jumbo frames, and "VLAN" to include tagging protocols such as 802.1Q and 802.1ad.

The PW termination point receives untagged ("raw") or tagged frames and delivers them unaltered to the termination point on the remote endpoint. A Native Service Processing (NSP) function sits between the Ethernet interface and the PW. It may strip, overwrite or add VLAN tags. The physical layer and the NSP functions are outside the scope of the RFC.
sections.plainLanguage: It is like a very long invisible cable between two rooms. What you put in one end comes out the other end looking the same.

sections.title: Setting Up the Control Connection and Sessions
sections.content:
Ethernet PWs are L2TPv3 sessions. The two endpoints (LCCEs, L2TP Control Connection Endpoints) MUST first establish an L2TP Control Connection as described in RFC 3931. Its Pseudowire Capabilities List must include an Ethernet PW type, either "Ethernet port" or "Ethernet VLAN". Connecting two ports requires the first type, and connecting two VLANs requires the second.

Provisioning an Ethernet port or VLAN and tying it to a PW triggers the standard Incoming Call three-way handshake (ICRQ, ICRP, ICCN). The Outgoing Call messages are not used, because they are mainly used for dial-up with L2TPv2 and have not been found applicable to PWs.

  • The Pseudowire Type AVP MUST be present in the ICRQ.
  • The Remote End Identifier AVP carries the Pseudowire ID and MUST be present in the ICRQ, so the peer can tell which PW the session belongs to. Implementations MUST support a four-octet identifier known to both ends by manual configuration or other means.
  • The Circuit Status AVP MUST be included in the ICRQ and ICRP, marked as a new circuit.
sections.plainLanguage: Before mailing anything, the two rooms call each other, agree what kind of cable they are pretending to be, and give it a shared name so both know which cable it is.

sections.title: Monitoring Status of the Pseudowire
sections.content:
The state of the L2TPv3 session reflects the working status of the PW. If the session is down, the PW MUST be shut down. The Control Connection keep-alive of L2TPv3 can monitor links for all PWs on a Control Connection.

The Set-Link-Info (SLI) message adds Ethernet link status notifications between the endpoints without bringing down the L2TP session. A change in an Ethernet interface triggers one SLI per associated PW, which may be one port PW or several VLAN PWs. The SLI MUST be sent any time a value in the Circuit Status AVP changes, except for the initial ICRQ, ICRP and CDN messages that set up and tear down the session itself.

The Circuit Status AVP value is a 16-bit mask. Only the two least significant bits are defined, and reserved bits MUST be set to 0 when sending and ignored on receipt. The A (Active) bit is 1 when the Ethernet interface is ACTIVE and 0 when INACTIVE. The N (New) bit is 1 for a new circuit and 0 for an existing one. In the ICCN and SLI, the N bit MUST indicate an existing circuit.
sections.plainLanguage: The two rooms keep telling each other whether their end of the cable is plugged in, so neither one is left talking into a dead line.

sections.title: Encapsulation, Sequencing and MTU
sections.content:
The entire Ethernet frame, without the preamble or frame check sequence (FCS), is encapsulated in L2TPv3 and sent as a single packet by the ingress endpoint. This happens whether or not a VLAN tag is present. In port-to-port mode the remote endpoint decapsulates the payload and sends it out without changing the Ethernet header. In VLAN-to-VLAN mode it MAY rewrite the VLAN tag. Both ends of a PW must be homogeneous: both tagged or both untagged.

Data packet sequencing MAY be enabled, using the mechanisms and signalling of RFC 3931.

The encapsulated IP packet is longer than the Ethernet frame by the IP header (with options and extension headers) plus N bytes. N covers the session header, a session ID of 4 octets, a cookie of 0, 4 or 8 octets and a 0 or 4 octet L2-specific sublayer (4 when sequencing). The RFC gives N as 4 to 16 octets over IP and 16 to 28 octets over UDP, not counting the IP header.

Fragmentation in the packet network can occur unless MTU sizes are properly managed between the customer and provider routers and across the network. Implementations MUST follow the fragmentation and reassembly guidelines of RFC 3931 and RFC 4623.
sections.plainLanguage: The whole message goes into one envelope, but the envelope adds a little weight. If the envelope grows too big for the mail slot, it has to be cut up, so the sizes need planning.

sections.title: What the Emulation Does and Does Not Preserve
sections.content:
The applicability statement describes how a PW compares with native Ethernet. A port PW connects two port attachment circuits and a VLAN PW connects two VLAN ones, both carrying variable-length frames in both directions. Because the FCS is not carried, payload integrity transparency may be lost. To get it back, the L2TPv3 session can use IPsec as RFC 3931 specifies.

The network may reorder, duplicate or silently drop packets, so sequencing can be enabled for some or all packets to detect lost, duplicate or out-of-order ones for each session. The maximum frame size is limited by the network MTU minus the L2TPv3 header size, unless fragmentation and reassembly is used.

Faithfulness can be improved with Quality-of-Service features. For 802.1Q transport, the ingress endpoint MAY use the user priority field to pick the Differentiated Services field of the outer IP header, and the egress endpoint MAY do the reverse. The mapping itself is application specific and out of scope.
sections.plainLanguage: The pretend cable is very good but not perfect. Mail can arrive late or out of order, and the check-number on each message is thrown away on the way.

sections.title: Congestion, Security and IANA
sections.content:
This specification offers no congestion control and is not TCP friendly. Because a PW can carry many kinds of traffic, it may not behave in a TCP-friendly manner and may take more than its fair share. Whenever possible, PWs should run over traffic-engineered networks with bandwidth allocation and admission control, such as IntServ or DiffServ domains.

Endpoints SHOULD monitor for congestion, by explicit congestion notification or by measuring packet loss. When severe congestion is detected, the PW SHOULD be halted by tearing down the L2TP session with a CDN message. It may be restarted manually or automatically after a waiting time. Thresholds and time periods need careful configuration to avoid losing service to temporary congestion and to prevent oscillation between congested and halted states.

For security, Ethernet over L2TPv3 is subject to all the general security considerations of RFC 3931. For IANA, the Pseudowire Types used are 0x0004 (Ethernet VLAN) and 0x0005 (Ethernet), allocated from the space created by RFC 3931.
sections.plainLanguage: If the road gets jammed, the cable-pretender cannot slow itself down politely, so it is told to stop for a while and try again later.
